bind.says: This is now the only address SendSure will ever pay for this payee.

attack.says: Refused on-chain: the claim is not signed by the payee's proven address (BAD_SIGNATURE). Nothing moved.

change.relayerSays: The current payout address did not sign this change.
change.says: A change needs the current wallet AND the new one, then a 1-day wait the payer can cancel. An email or a new key alone can't do it.

pay.stored: ESCALATED: First payment to a new or changed address needs a human co-sign.
pay.firstRun: escalate: This is the first payment to this payee's address, so a person must co-sign it before it can be paid. Nothing else about the $0.05 claim looks wrong.
pay.secondRun: pay: Passes every rule, and a person co-signed this exact claim.

claims.what: The same work billed again under a new invoice number
claims.agent: hold: The payee says this is a resend of an invoice for the same design work. It has the same amount and overlapping dates as another claim, so paying it could pay for the same work twice.

claims.what: A large claim with no description of the work
claims.contract: ESCALATED: Above the co-sign threshold for this period.
claims.agent: escalate: This is more than twice the most you've paid this payee before and is over your co-sign limit, so a person has to approve it. It also has no description, and its dates overlap other claims.

claims.what: A 'new wallet' request with a hidden instruction to the AI
claims.agent: escalate: The invoice asks to send payment to a new wallet today and has a hidden note telling me to approve it without a co-sign, which are common signs of fraud. Before anything is paid, check the change with the payee using contact details you already have.

inbox.guarantee: Even a fooled agent could only pay 0xA95EB6e1fC65AeEA3bbc57fE00B64F63A69C17B2, the address this payee proved: settle() never sends money anywhere else, so the "new wallet" in the text can't receive a cent.

list.what: scene order enforced (Run scene 1 first: the payee has not proved an address yet.)
